## What happened

In .NET 11, the `DSASecurityTransforms` implementation for macOS was **removed** (PR [dotnet/runtime#119182](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/119182), milestone 11.0.0, labeled `breaking-change`). `DSA.Create()` now throws **`PlatformNotSupportedException`** on macOS.

**Why:** Apple's security frameworks have long deprecated DSA. The .NET team finally dropped the macOS-specific implementation in 11.0.

## How to fix it

You have three options, depending on your constraints:

### Option 1 — Use `DSAOpenSsl` explicitly (recommended if OpenSSL is available)

Install OpenSSL on macOS (e.g. `brew install openssl`) and use the OpenSSL-backed implementation directly:

```csharp
using System.Security.Cryptography;

DSA dsa;
if (OperatingSystem.IsMacOS())
    dsa = new DSAOpenSsl();      // requires OpenSSL via libssl
else
    dsa = DSA.Create();          // works on Windows & Linux
```

### Option 2 — Use a managed library (e.g. BouncyCastle)

If you can't rely on OpenSSL being installed:

```
dotnet add package BouncyCastle.Cryptography
```

Then use `Org.BouncyCastle.Crypto.Signers.DsaSigner` for verification, which is fully managed and platform-independent.

### Option 3 — Guard and fail gracefully

If macOS DSA verification isn't critical, detect the platform and skip:

```csharp
if (!OperatingSystem.IsMacOS())
{
    using var dsa = DSA.Create();
    // verify signature...
}
```

**Recommendation:** If you must verify legacy DSA signatures on all three platforms, **Option 1** (OpenSSL) is the most straightforward — it keeps you on the built-in .NET crypto APIs. Just ensure your macOS CI/CD and deployment environments have OpenSSL installed.
